3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/tui"
10	)
11	
12	// consent.go is phase 4's gate. Distilling sessions into durable facts is the
13	// only part of setup that spends money, and until this file existed it was
14	// opt-OUT: a first run distilled unless the operator happened to know about
15	// --no-backfill.
16	//
17	// Two properties matter more than the wording:
18	//
19	//   - DEFAULT NO. Bare Enter, EOF, a closed stdin, garbage twice: all skip.
20	//     Silence is never consent to spend.
21	//   - NEVER BLOCK WITHOUT A TERMINAL. A prompt in CI is a wedged pipeline, and
22	//     a wedged pipeline is a worse outcome than any amount of unspent budget.
23	//     The no-TTY path does not read stdin AT ALL — not a byte, not a peek —
24	//     which is a stronger and far more testable claim than "it defaults".
25	
26	// Override is an explicit instruction from a flag, which suppresses the prompt.
27	type Override int
28	
29	const (
30		// OverrideNone leaves the decision to the prompt.
31		OverrideNone Override = iota
32		// OverrideYes is --yes: the only way to spend without a human.
33		OverrideYes
34		// OverrideNo is --no-backfill.
35		OverrideNo
36	)
37	
38	// ConsentRequest is everything the gate needs. It carries the TTY capability
39	// explicitly rather than sniffing a file descriptor, so every path through
40	// this function is reachable from a unit test.
41	type ConsentRequest struct {
42		// Compact uses the short setup prompt instead of the verbose phase block.
43		Compact bool
44		// Sessions is how many sessions THIS run would distill: the pending pool
45		// capped by the spend budget. The cost estimate is derived from it.
46		Sessions int
47		// Total is the whole pending pool before the budget cap. When it exceeds
48		// Sessions, the prompt says both numbers — a reader deciding whether to
49		// spend needs to know the pool is 272 even when this run covers 2.
50		Total int
51		// Covered is how many sessions team memories already cover (fact
52		// provenance from the hosted store); Corpus is the whole session count.
53		// When Covered > 0 the prompt says so — the reader deciding whether to
54		// spend should know most of the corpus needs nothing.
55		Covered int
56		Corpus  int
57		// Agent is the agent CLI that would run. Empty means none was found.
58		Agent string
59		// Model and Effort qualify the agent, for the informed-decision line.
60		Model  string
61		Effort string
62		// Override is the flag, if one was passed.
63		Override Override
64		// TTY reports whether a human can answer.
65		TTY bool
66		// ResumeCommand is the one command that starts a distill later. It is
67		// printed on every skip, because a skip that does not say how to change
68		// its mind is a dead end.
69		ResumeCommand string
70	}
71	
72	// ConsentReason is WHY consent landed where it did, as a value.
73	//
74	// Reason below is a sentence for a human. Anything that needs to branch on the
75	// outcome must branch on this instead: the short form has to tell "no agent on
76	// PATH" apart from "the human said no", and deriving that by matching English
77	// against Reason breaks the moment the sentence is reworded.
78	type ConsentReason int
79	
80	const (
81		// ConsentReasonUnset is the zero value; treat it as "not decided here".
82		ConsentReasonUnset ConsentReason = iota
83		// ConsentReasonNoBackfill is --no-backfill.
84		ConsentReasonNoBackfill
85		// ConsentReasonNoSessions is a repo with nothing recorded yet.
86		ConsentReasonNoSessions
87		// ConsentReasonNoAgent is sessions present and no CLI able to read them.
88		ConsentReasonNoAgent
89		// ConsentReasonFlagYes is --yes.
90		ConsentReasonFlagYes
91		// ConsentReasonNoTTY is a non-interactive stdin, where silence is not
92		// consent.
93		ConsentReasonNoTTY
94		// ConsentReasonAccepted is a human who answered yes.
95		ConsentReasonAccepted
96		// ConsentReasonDeclined is a human who answered no.
97		ConsentReasonDeclined
98	
99		// The four below are reached BEFORE consent is asked, so they are not
100		// consent decisions at all -- they are the reasons the question never
101		// came up. They live in this enum because the short form needs one typed
102		// answer to "why was nothing distilled", and inventing a second enum for
103		// half of it would just move the matching problem.
104	
105		// ConsentReasonPaused is `brain stop`: background work is paused, and
106		// re-running setup will skip again. The remedy is `start`.
107		ConsentReasonPaused
108		// ConsentReasonAlreadyDistilled is a re-run with nothing pending.
109		ConsentReasonAlreadyDistilled
110		// ConsentReasonAlreadyRunning is a backfill already in flight. Reporting
111		// this as "skipped" contradicts the machine's actual state.
112		ConsentReasonAlreadyRunning
113		// ConsentReasonNoExecutable is an unresolvable path to this binary, so
114		// nothing could be spawned.
115		ConsentReasonNoExecutable
116	)
117	
118	// ConsentOutcome is the decision and why it was reached.
119	type ConsentOutcome struct {
120		// Spend is the answer.
121		Spend bool
122		// Reason is always set, including when Spend is true. It is what the
123		// settled phase line says.
124		Reason string
125		// Why is the same decision as a value, for callers that must branch.
126		Why ConsentReason
127		// Prompted reports whether a human was actually asked. A test asserting
128		// "CI does not block" asserts on this, not on the answer.
129		Prompted bool
130	}
131	
132	// DefaultResumeCommand is the command printed when a distill is skipped.
133	const DefaultResumeCommand = "entire brain distill"
134	
135	// Consent decides whether phase 4 may spend.
136	//
137	// Order is load bearing. The three "spending is impossible" checks come first,
138	// so --yes in a repo with no sessions and no agent reports the truth instead of
139	// claiming it spent. Then the flags, then the terminal. The reader `in` is
140	// touched on exactly one path: a real prompt on a real terminal.
141	func Consent(req ConsentRequest, in io.Reader, out io.Writer, r *Renderer) ConsentOutcome {
142		resume := req.ResumeCommand
143		if strings.TrimSpace(resume) == "" {
144			resume = DefaultResumeCommand
145		}
146	
147		switch {
148		// Nothing to distill comes FIRST. The flag declines work; it cannot
149		// decline work that does not exist, and "not distilled (--no-backfill)"
150		// to someone whose repo has no captured sessions reports a decision
151		// instead of explaining the state.
152		case req.Sessions <= 0:
153			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "no sessions to distill; the brain is queryable now", Why: ConsentReasonNoSessions}
154		case req.Override == OverrideNo:
155			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled (--no-backfill); start later: " + resume, Why: ConsentReasonNoBackfill}
156		case req.Agent == "":
157			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "no agent CLI on PATH, nothing can distill; " + RemedyAgent, Why: ConsentReasonNoAgent}
158		case req.Override == OverrideYes:
159			return ConsentOutcome{Spend: true, Reason: "distilling " + plural(req.Sessions, "session") + " (--yes)", Why: ConsentReasonFlagYes}
160		case !req.TTY:
161			// Not a prompt, not a read, not a wait: one line and a default.
162			return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled: no terminal to ask, and silence is not consent; run " + resume + " or pass --yes", Why: ConsentReasonNoTTY}
163		}
164	
165		blockLines := writePrompt(out, r, req)
166		answer, prompted, promptLines := askTwice(in, out, r, req.Compact)
167		erasePrompt(out, blockLines+promptLines)
168		if answer {
169			return ConsentOutcome{Spend: true, Reason: "distilling " + plural(req.Sessions, "session") + ", newest first", Why: ConsentReasonAccepted, Prompted: prompted}
170		}
171		return ConsentOutcome{Reason: "not distilled; the brain is queryable now, start later: " + resume, Why: ConsentReasonDeclined, Prompted: prompted}
172	}
173	
174	// writePrompt paints the block the operator is answering. It uses the same
175	// gutter as every phase line, with the glyph column left blank: a question is
176	// not an outcome and must not wear an outcome's tick.
177	func writePrompt(out io.Writer, r *Renderer, req ConsentRequest) int {
178		if out == nil {
179			return 0
180		}
181		bullet := " " + r.Bullet() + " "
182		agent := "Agent: " + req.Agent
183		if req.Model != "" {
184			agent += bullet + "model: " + req.Model
185		}
186		if req.Effort != "" {
187			agent += bullet + "effort: " + req.Effort
188		}
189		if req.Compact {
190			pool := max(req.Total, req.Sessions)
191			verb := "remain"
192			if pool == 1 {
193				verb = "remains"
194			}
195			count := 0
196			for i, text := range []string{
197				fmt.Sprintf("%s %s. Distill up to %d now?", plural(pool, "session"), verb, req.Sessions),
198				agent + bullet + "uses agent tokens",
199			} {
200				for _, line := range r.Wrap(text) {
201					if i > 0 {
202						line = r.TUI().Paint(tui.CLIMuted, line)
203					}
204					fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", line)
205					count++
206				}
207			}
208			return count
209		}
210		pool := plural(req.Sessions, "session")
211		estimate := "Estimated: ~" + plural(req.Sessions, "agent call") + ", newest first, resumable."
212		if req.Total > req.Sessions {
213			pool = plural(req.Total, "session")
214			estimate = fmt.Sprintf("Estimated: ~%s this run (spend budget), newest first, resumable.",
215				plural(req.Sessions, "agent call"))
216		}
217		lines := []Line{
218			{Title: PhaseFacts.Title(), Text: pool + " can be distilled into durable facts.", Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
219		}
220		if req.Covered > 0 {
221			lines = append(lines, Line{
222				Text:   fmt.Sprintf("%d of %d sessions are already covered by team memories.", req.Covered, req.Corpus),
223				Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent(),
224			})
225		}
226		lines = append(lines,
227			Line{Text: agent, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
228			Line{Text: estimate, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()},
229			Line{Blank: true},
230		)
231		for _, line := range lines {
232			fmt.Fprintln(out, r.Line(line))
233		}
234		return len(lines)
235	}
236	
237	// erasePrompt clears the consent block once it is answered. The question must
238	// be ASKED — it gates token spend — but it does not have to be KEPT: after the
239	// answer the block is history, and the final summary should be the only output
240	// left on the operator's terminal. Only the real-terminal path reaches this,
241	// so the ANSI is safe; lines counts the block plus one line per prompt attempt
242	// (the operator's Enter completed each).
243	func erasePrompt(out io.Writer, lines int) {
244		if out == nil || lines <= 0 {
245			return
246		}
247		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\x1b[%dA\x1b[J", lines)
248	}
249	
250	// question is the prompt itself. "[y/N]" is not decoration: the capital is the
251	// default, and it is the default.
252	const question = "Distill now? [y/N]"
253	
254	// askTwice reads an answer, re-asking ONCE on something unrecognisable and
255	// defaulting to No after that. Two chances is the whole budget: a loop here is
256	// a different way of blocking a pipeline.
257	func askTwice(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, r *Renderer, compact bool) (answer, prompted bool, lines int) {
258		if in == nil {
259			return false, false, 0
260		}
261		reader := bufio.NewReader(in)
262		promptLine := func(text string) string {
263			if compact {
264				return "  " + text
265			}
266			return r.Line(Line{Text: text, Accent: PhaseFacts.Accent()})
267		}
268		for attempt := 0; attempt < 2; attempt++ {
269			// Printed with a trailing space Line would have trimmed: the cursor has to
270			// sit clear of the "]" or the answer reads as part of the question.
271			fmt.Fprint(out, promptLine(question)+" ")
272			// The operator's Enter (or the explicit newline on EOF) completes the
273			// prompt line, so each attempt occupies exactly one line for the erase.
274			lines++
275			line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
276			got := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
277			if err != nil && got == "" {
278				// EOF, a closed stdin, an interrupt that shut the pipe: No, with a
279				// newline so the next line does not land beside the prompt.
280				fmt.Fprintln(out)
281				return false, true, lines
282			}
283			switch got {
284			case "y", "yes":
285				return true, true, lines
286			case "", "n", "no":
287				return false, true, lines
288			}
289			if attempt == 0 {
290				fmt.Fprintln(out, promptLine("Please answer y or n."))
291				lines++
292			}
293			if err != nil {
294				fmt.Fprintln(out)
295				return false, true, lines
296			}
297		}
298		return false, true, lines
299	}

content.thinking:
I've got Consent fully in view now, and for Task 3 I'm leaning toward a bubbletea-based `Select` prompt that keeps the same contract style: explicit TTY flag, default handling, erase-after. The design says consent should ride that same stack, but its current reader-based version is deliberately simple and heavily tested, so moving its interactive branch over needs care about how bubbletea reads from the `in` reader.

I'm weighing whether moving consent's interactive branch onto bubbletea is worth the risk. Bubbletea can read from the `in` reader and handle raw mode on a real TTY, but it takes over the terminal and its erase and line accounting could disturb the carefully tested consent gate. The design asks for one prompt style everywhere, yet the plan's step to re-implement consent as a two-option confirm with default No and the Override short-circuit unchanged may be the safer path.

I'm sketching a shared bubbletea model for both prompts, with up/down/j/k to move, enter to answer, and esc/q/ctrl+c to abort, plus per-option key shortcuts so consent can keep its y/n typing. Consent's interactive branch would then run through that model with tea.WithInput(in), while the rest of the flow stays as it is.

I'm weighing whether bubbletea can read y/n keystrokes from the `in` reader without breaking the existing consent tests that feed in strings like "y\n". Testing the model's Update and View directly, and only running a full tea.Program on the production path, looks like the safer way to keep those tests stable.

I'm worried that bubbletea would hang on finite input buffers, since it never quits on reader EOF, so I'm leaning toward keeping Consent's line-reader implementation as the safer ruling.

I'm now weighing a middle path: keep consent's line-reader as it is, since it already shares the Renderer and palette, and build only the new Select prompt on bubbletea. That departs from the design's "same stack" line, so I'm considering a numbered-choice Select without bubbletea as the alternative.

I'm settling on Select using bubbletea only for real TTY interaction, and leaving the no-TTY path to return unanswered without starting a program. For consent, the open question is whether the existing buffer-fed tests with TTY set would hang once the interactive branch moves to bubbletea, since bubbletea doesn't quit on reader EOF.

I'm settling on keeping Consent's reader loop as it is, since its semantics and tests depend on it, and building only the new Select prompt on bubbletea for interactive choices. The visual consistency still holds because both go through the same Renderer, palette, and gutter. That's a departure from the design's "same stack" line, so I'll flag it for the user, and I'll test the no-TTY path of Select separately.

Now I'm defining the selection prompt: a small options struct with label, detail, and key, plus a request that carries the default index and the TTY flag. For a non-TTY or empty option list it returns the default straight away, and otherwise it starts a bubbletea program on the given input and output.

Writing the Select result handling now: if the program errors or the user never answered, it falls back to the default index, and otherwise it returns the cursor position as answered.

Next I'm wrapping up the Select model's key handling: enter answers and quits, while esc, ctrl+c and q abort without answering, and a pressed option shortcut picks that option directly. Then I'm sketching the tests, covering arrow-then-enter selection, esc meaning unanswered, the shortcut key choosing an option, and a no-TTY call that never writes escape codes.

I'm going to check the bubbletea import path and version in go.mod, since the API differs between v1 and v2. The dash package already uses it in internal/tui/tui.go, so I'll look at how that file imports and calls it.

I'm keeping the consent gate's line-reader loop for Task 3, since its no-block and default-No-on-EOF guarantees are test-pinned and bubbletea hangs on reader EOF. The new interactive select will be pure bubbletea, and I'll flag this deviation in the final summary.
